activities.description: Melissa takes Greg's patient history. They discuss his hearing trouble, particularly in background noise, and his exposure to live music.

characterInteraction.description: Melissa takes a friendly and professional lead, asking open-ended questions to gather information about Greg's hearing difficulties and potential causes.

mood.description: Calm, professional. The soft lighting and neutral colors of the room contribute to a calming atmosphere. Melissa's friendly and professional demeanor creates a sense of trust.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of the patient and his reason for seeking an audiometry test.

scenes.thematicElements: Importance of a detailed patient history in audiological assessments.
scenes.title: Introduction & Patient History

videoEditingDetails.description: Title card with University of Canterbury logo and text: 'Department of Communication Disorders', 'Adult Audiometry'.

activities.description: Melissa performs otoscopy on both of Greg's ears, examining the ear canals for wax or other debris.

characterInteraction.description: Melissa continues to be professional, explaining the process and ensuring Greg is comfortable.

mood.description: Calm, clinical. The close-up shots of the ear examination create a more clinical mood.

narrativeProgression.description: Visual demonstration of the otoscopy process, an essential part of an audiometry test.

scenes.thematicElements: Importance of otoscopy in identifying conditions that may impact hearing.
scenes.title: Otoscopy

activities.description: Melissa explains and performs tympanometry to assess Greg's middle ear function.

characterInteraction.description: Melissa provides a clear explanation of the tympanometry procedure to Greg, helping him understand what to expect.

mood.description: Calm, informative. Melissa clearly explains the procedure.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of tympanometry as a way to assess middle ear function.

scenes.thematicElements: The role of immittance audiometry in evaluating the middle ear system.
scenes.title: Immittance Audiometry: Tympanometry

activities.description: Melissa explains the audiogram procedure and instructs Greg on how to use the response button.
Melissa conducts air conduction pure-tone testing, establishing Greg's hearing thresholds for various frequencies.

characterInteraction.description: Melissa guides Greg through the audiogram procedure, offering clear instructions and encouragement.

mood.description: Calm, focused. The sound booth creates a sense of isolation for accurate testing, and Melissa is focused on administering the test.

narrativeProgression.description: Explanation and demonstration of the audiogram process, showing how hearing thresholds are determined for different frequencies.
Melissa explains that Greg will be hearing beeps one ear at a time and that he should press the red button whenever he hears one, even if it is very soft.
The client responds to the sounds by pressing a response button.
The test establishes the patient’s threshold of hearing for each of a number of frequencies important for understanding speech.
The audiologist starts at an intensity level that is easily audible to the client.
This is repeated until the client has responded to two out of three ascending presentations.
On the audiogram, the thresholds are recorded as crosses for the left ear and circles for the right ear.

props.name: Audiometer with a screen displaying test parameters.

scenes.thematicElements: The significance of pure-tone audiometry in evaluating hearing sensitivity across a range of frequencies.
scenes.title: Audiogram: Pure-Tone Testing (Air Conduction)

videoEditingDetails.description: Visual change: The audiometer screen’s volume display is highlighted as the narrator explains what that number means.

activities.description: Melissa explains and conducts bone conduction testing to further assess Greg's hearing loss and identify the site of lesion.
Melissa reviews the audiogram results with Greg, explaining his hearing levels across different frequencies.

characterInteraction.description: Melissa continues to maintain a professional and supportive interaction with Greg, explaining the purpose of the bone conduction testing and the significance of the findings.

mood.description: Calm, reassuring. Melissa explains the results clearly.

narrativeProgression.description: Bone conduction testing is used to determine if the hearing loss is in the cochlea. Explanation of Greg's audiogram results, indicating a mild-to-moderate high-frequency hearing loss in both ears.

scenes.thematicElements: The importance of bone conduction testing in differentiating between conductive and sensorineural hearing loss. The impact of high-frequency hearing loss on understanding speech.
scenes.title: Audiogram: Bone Conduction Testing

activities.description: Melissa explains that she will prepare a formal report with a copy of the results and send them to Greg via mail.

characterInteraction.description: Melissa concludes the assessment with a professional farewell, ensuring Greg understands the next steps.

narrativeProgression.description: Closing of the appointment with a clear explanation of the follow-up steps.

scenes.thematicElements: The importance of providing clear and comprehensive follow-up information to clients.
scenes.title: Conclusion & Follow-up

climax.description: The audiogram results are revealed and discussed, indicating the nature of Greg's hearing loss.

storylines.description: The video chronicles an adult audiometry assessment, presenting the steps from patient intake to the review of audiogram results.

content_metadata.title: Adult Audiometry: An Experiential Overview

trimmingSuggestions.description: The otoscopy scene could be slightly trimmed. While important, extended close-ups of the ear canal might be less engaging for viewers.
The tympanometry scene could also be shortened, focusing on the essential aspects of the explanation and procedure.
